newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee market slips, trade near standstill.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee market slips, trade near standstill.

text.p: Vietnamese coffee prices have followed the New York and London markets lower in the past week, but trade has remained at a near standstill as traders wait for stock from the 1996/97 crop to kick in.
Traders said on Friday that buyers were bidding at around $1,230 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, down some $70 from early September, while sellers were looking for about $1,250.
However, they said the prices were largely indicative.
"There's very little demand for Vietnam's coffee right now. Indonesian coffee prices are looking better, so that's where buyers are looking," said one.
Another trader said that although remaining stocks were low -- an estimated 3,000 tonnes -- some farmers with coffee still to sell had been holding back in the hope of getting better prices.
"They must be getting scared now because the new crop is coming," she said.
Harvesting of the next crop has already got under way in some areas, but harvesting of the bulk is not expected to start until mid-October.
The 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) crop was estimated at 180,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
